title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 3° treats the stable compactification M̂_{0,5} = M̄_{0,5}, written M̂_{0,I} with I a 5-element set of labels, by the same method as the previous section (which computed the class of M_{1,1} in K_!(Z)).

Table (81) lists the strata by the combinatorial type of the dual tree:
- codim 0: one vertex carrying all 5 points.
- codim 1: two vertices, with a split I = I'(2) ⊔ I''(3).
- codim 2: a chain of three vertices with 2, 1 and 2 points.

The arrow labels give the incidence numbers. The open stratum specializes to 10 divisors, one for each 2-subset I'. Each divisor contains 3 codim-2 points.

Each boundary divisor D_{I'} is canonically identified with M̂_{0,I''⊔{*}}, a copy of M̂_{0,4}. Writing P^1_{I''} := P^1_Z ∧^{Isom({0,1,∞},I'')} S_3, this is the twist of P^1_Z by the S_3-torsor of identifications of {0,1,∞} with I''. So it is a canonical, label-free projective line whose three special points are indexed by I''.

Counting and incidence:
- Points at infinity: 10·3/2 = 15. They correspond to the partitions of I of type (2,2,1).
- D_{I'} and D_{J'} meet iff I'∩J' = ∅, i.e. iff I', J', I∖(I'∪J') is a (2,2,1) partition.
- So the intersection graph of the boundary is the Kneser graph K(5,2), the Petersen graph.

Grothendieck then uses the combinatorics of the icosahedron. An orientation of I (a choice of A_5-class) fixes an icosahedral structure on the S_5 ≅ A_5-symmetry. The continuation is on the next page:
- The 10 divisors correspond to the 10 'triangles' I∖I'. These are the faces of the 'icosaèdre gauche', i.e. the hemi-icosahedron (pairs of opposite faces).
- The 15 (2,2,1)-partitions are read as 'square structures' on 4 of the 5 points. They correspond to the 15 edges.
- By duality, the stratification of M̄_{0,5} matches the vertices and edges of the hemi-dodecahedron.

The purpose is to describe the 'structure à l'infini' of M̂_{0,5} combinatorially and S_5-equivariantly. This is presumably preparing an Euler-characteristic or K_!-class computation analogous to formula (80) for M_{1,1}.
errors: No mathematical errors. All counts check: 10 divisors, 3 points on each, each point on 2 divisors, so 15 points. Meeting iff the 2-subsets are disjoint. The (10) and (3) incidence labels are correct.

The phrase 'choosing an orientation of I determines an icosahedron' is stated without justification. It is correct up to the outer automorphism of S_5: an orientation selects one of the two conjugacy classes of icosahedral embeddings.

ideas.what: Stratification of M̄_{0,5} by dual trees, with incidence numbers 10 and 3.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,5} and the boundary 'à l'infini' qualitatively

ideas.what: Each boundary divisor of M̄_{0,5} is the twisted P^1 obtained from P^1_Z by contracted product with the S_3-torsor Isom({0,1,∞},I'').
ideas.modern_name: Canonical identification of a boundary divisor with M̄_{0,4} ≅ P^1 (gluing map)

ideas.what: The dual intersection graph of the boundary of M̄_{0,5} is the Kneser graph K(5,2) (Petersen graph); the 15 nodes correspond to (2,2,1)-partitions.
ideas.modern_name: Petersen graph as boundary complex of M̄_{0,5}; equivalently the 10 lines on the quintic del Pezzo surface
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (lines on the degree-5 del Pezzo surface); modern tropical/boundary-complex literature

ideas.what: Identification of the boundary combinatorics with the hemi-icosahedron (faces, edges) and dually the hemi-dodecahedron (vertices, edges), via an icosahedral structure on the 5-set I.
ideas.modern_name: Petersen graph = 1-skeleton of the hemi-dodecahedron; S_5 / A_5 icosahedral combinatorics

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly describes the boundary combinatorics of M̂_{0,5} through the hemi-icosahedron and hemi-dodecahedron, S_5-equivariantly after fixing an orientation of I. This is a personal, unpublished presentation of a classically known fact (Petersen graph = hemi-dodecahedron graph = intersection graph of the 10 lines on the quintic del Pezzo surface). It is not a new result.
missed.quote: D'après l'étude combinatoire de l'icosaèdre, choisissant une orientation de I — ce qui détermine un icosaèdre orienté
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's polyhedral and Platonic viewpoint on the Teichmüller tower (also seen in his dessins work). Historically interesting, but mathematically known.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard boundary combinatorics of M̄_{0,5} (Petersen graph). The icosahedral/dodecahedral reinterpretation is a classical fact, though nice to see in Grothendieck's hand and linked to his K_!-class computations.
transcription_corrections: The marginal definition reads approximately 'P^1_{I''} =def P^1_Z ∧^{Isom} S_3'. The torsor is Isom({0,1,∞}, I''), not 'ℓ'(...)'.
In the line under (81), the object is likely 'Isom({0,1,∞},I'')' rather than 'ℓ'({0,1,∞},I'')'.
'dont chacun est un M̂^!_{0,4}' — each divisor is an M̂^!_{0,4}, more precisely M̂_{0,I''(3)⊔(*)} ≃ (P^1_{I''})_Z.
The number '32' at the top is Grothendieck's own pagination. '65' at the bottom left is the archive page number.
